B: A faded banner, turned to face the wall: the open hand holding a sword by the blade.
t: Long tables, scrubbed clean. Horde and townsfolk eat here side by side and pretend not to see each other.
k: A candle that never burns down. Rest here.
L: A tally over the bar: DAYS SINCE THE HORDE PAID FOR A DRINK: 182,621.
b: A bed. Clean sheets. Somebody still cares about this place.
1: The door back to the street.

objects.name: Nana Birch
lines: Sit. Eat. You're too thin. Everyone's too thin.
I feed the horde too. A full belly swings a slower axe.

answer: The king hasn't aged a day since my great-great-grandmother's time. Nobody finds that odd. I find that odd.

questions.ask: Tell me about the old days.
answer: My family kept an inn for the old king, too. The Hales. A king who asked the cook how the soup was.
Mad as a bag of cats by the end, they say. But he asked about the soup.
Because you can't carry anyone if you can't carry yourself. Now eat.
Turnip. Millbrook sends them. The horde won't touch a turnip, so nobody asks where they go.
Half this town's lived on Millbrook turnips for years. So will you. Eat.

lines: A little door behind the tables, chalked: POTATOES.
It's warm behind it, and it smells of people. Not of potatoes.

objects.name: Oren
lines: Oren. I've been sitting here a while. The inn is quiet. Quiet is good. Sit, if you like.
